maria (sec-eng): heads up — Legal just forwarded a DSAR that asks for deletion of all personal data, explicitly calling out vector embeddings and backups across regions. asking how we prove deletion to them.
akash (infra): ok — do we know which storage/backups contain embeddings for that tenant?
jordan (privacy): they want proof of deletion within 30 days and a signed attestation. we can provide logs + deletion ops but need to confirm cross-region snapshot behavior.
riley (platform): @maria, do we have an index of embedding locations per customer? I think embeddings live in: 1) vector DB primary (redis/pgvector), 2) S3 blob snapshots (periodic snapshots), 3) long-term archive in object store for backups.
maria (sec-eng): yep that's right. question: if snapshots are encrypted with our KMS key, is disabling the key enough to satisfy deletion?
akash (infra): short answer: disabling a KMS key prevents new decrypts via the key but ciphertext still exists. disabling isn't a lawful deletion proof, legal will push back.
jordan (privacy): legal won't accept "we disabled a key". they want demonstrable deletion of the data or an allowed retention exception.
maria (sec-eng): what about physically deleting the S3 objects and snapshot manifest entries? is that something we can run across regions?
akash (infra): we can. plan: 1) list objects per snapshot, 2) run targeted deletes, 3) update snapshot manifests, 4) trigger bucket replication deletes. also must ensure restore points (glacier vaults) — may require vendor support.
ops-bot: deploy started: deletion-runner v2.3 triggered by maria at 2025-11-02T14:12:03Z
riley (platform): We need an RBAC change so only the deletion-runner service account has the delete_s3_objects permission and a time-limited grant. ops should add an auditable annotation to each delete op with request_id and dsar_id.
maria (sec-eng): agreed. what's the minimal RBAC delta?
akash (infra): new role: data-erasure-runner with s3:DeleteObject on specific buckets + snapshots:DeleteSnapshot. attach to deletion-runner SA with expiration 7d. also require kms:GenerateDataKey? actually deletion won't need decrypt — just delete. keep keys untouched.
jordan (privacy): legal wants a canonical chain-of-custody artifact. propose we produce a single signed JSON manifest that includes: dsar_id, list of deleted object keys, deletion_timestamps, operator (service account), sha256 of object prior to delete (if we captured digest), and storage-provider deletion receipts.
maria (sec-eng): can we capture sha256 prior? we don't currently store it for vector blobs. we can record object size + ETag at least.
akash (infra): ETag + object size should be fine as evidence for object identity. for DB rows (vector indices) we can capture a pre-delete row count and sample ids.
riley (platform): here's a quick command to delete an S3 object and log receipt:
```bash
aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-embeddings-prod --key "customers/tenant-1234/emb-0001" \
  --expected-bucket-owner 123456789012 && echo "deleted: customers/tenant-1234/emb-0001" >> /var/log/erasure/1749991111.log
```
maria (sec-eng): for pgvector: we need to remove rows and vacuum. sample SQL:
```sql
BEGIN;
DELETE FROM embeddings WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant-1234';
SELECT count(*) FROM embeddings WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant-1234';
COMMIT;
```
akash (infra): important: snapshots taken after deletion might still include old data if the snapshot was created BEFORE the delete. need to delete snapshot objects separately. also for cross-region replication, deletion markers may be async — we should wait for replication confirmation.
jordan (privacy): also ask: does retention exception apply? if there's a legal hold for an investigation we may not delete. legal will tell us. for normal DSARs we should delete unless an exception exists.
maria (sec-eng): can we produce an attestation if some archive provider refuses immediate deletion (e.g., vendor SLA)?
akash (infra): we can provide: 1) our attempted deletion logs, 2) vendor ticket showing deletion request and vendor-side acknowledge timestamp, 3) status of any outstanding objects. that usually satisfies regulators if we show reasonable effort.
riley (platform): audit logging change: add a field to our platform audit record for erasure requests: { dsar_id, requester_email, operator_sa, objects_deleted[], snapshots_deleted[], vendor_receipts[] } — we should include a signature (HMAC) of the manifest.
maria (sec-eng): who will own the RBAC request? I can draft the change but need infra approval to apply short-lived role.
akash (infra): I'll review. pls include exact IAM policy lines. minimal example:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:DeleteObject","s3:DeleteObjectVersion"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-embeddings-prod/*"]}
  ]
}
```
jordan (privacy): I'll prepare language for the attestation template that Legal signs after we produce receipts. includes statement that deletion was performed to the best of our technical ability and lists outstanding items (if any).
maria (sec-eng): one more: vuln triage angle — if DSAR references deleted data that was exfiltrated in an incident, we should mark this DSAR for incident response. add tag dsar:related-to-incident if confirmed.
riley (platform): added a ticket in infra: INF-8274 "DSAR erasure-runner: short-lived role + audit fields" assigned to akash.
ops-bot: ticket INF-8274 created by riley at 2025-11-02T14:20:10Z
maria (sec-eng): ok I'll start assembling the manifest template and list of object prefixes. tagging @jordan for legal language.
jordan (privacy): thanks — once you have the manifest draft I'll review and confirm acceptable attestations.
maria (sec-eng): plan of record: (1) create data-erasure-runner role with 7d expiry, (2) run targeted deletes for DB rows + S3 objects + snapshots, (3) collect vendor receipts, ETag/size, and deletion timestamps, (4) produce signed manifest and delivery to legal. aim to finish within 21 days unless legal requests faster.
akash (infra): will prep IAM policy & cross-region delete scripts. ping me when ready to run.
riley (platform): will shepherd audit schema change and ensure manifests are HMAC-signed.
maria (sec-eng): thanks all. I'll follow up with the manifest draft in this thread. :white_check_mark:
